text.literalString: How to Disclose a Felony/Recovery Before an Interview

A simple, effective pre-interview disclosure works best when it’s brief, honest, and future-focused. A helpful structure is: (1) signal transparency, (2) name the fact(s) without over-explaining, (3) emphasize readiness to work, and (4) ask a clear question about whether it’s a barrier.

Sample script (email/phone): “Before we go further, I want to be transparent: I’m in recovery, and I have a felony conviction from my past. I’m excited about the role and don’t want to waste your time—would this affect my eligibility to interview or move forward?”

Tips: keep it short; avoid detailed personal history; use calm, non-apologetic language; and ask directly about next steps (e.g., eligibility, background check policy, or required documentation).
